matches.text: A proposed connexion between thrombin binding non-additivity and quantum harmonic readout survives as a conditional contact-response diagnostic. This work found that exact coordinate reduction preserves shared-coordinate covariance but can reverse the sign of a retained harmonic stiffness cycle; an omitted-coordinate contribution restores the full cycle. The evidence concerns prescribed spring models, without molecular validation or demonstrated quantum advantage. The thread ended at PAUSE. Its first useful deliverable is a checked chemical map for 3B, 5B, 3F and 5F. Exact reduction checks, approximate spring-model tests and independent trajectory validation answer different questions. The estimator, calibration procedure, uncertainty choices and quantitative rejection threshold remain unresolved.

The thread ended at PAUSE, as specified in the brief. The scientific obstacle is the gap between checked mathematical representations and a validated molecular diagnostic. Completing the chemical map introduced in Section 1 would remove an immediate obstacle to defining \(S_{gh}\) in all four B/F states and forming \(D_{F;B}\). It would permit the next classical response comparison, without itself validating a model or establishing a molecular sign or ordering.\footnote{Research record: joint entries 17 and 30; branch-3 entry 71.}

This work asked whether better quantum optimisation of a docking score could resolve a thrombin binding discrepancy. It found a prerequisite problem: neither of two frozen contact representations improved prediction of 16 other ligands over training-only series means when larger scores were required to imply more favourable binding. One representation improved prediction with the opposite orientation. These descriptive results survive matched-substituent exclusions and the enumerated reference choices, but lack independent model-selection validation and experimental covariance. The thread ended at DRAFT. Candidate selection, access to untouched validation affinities and a replication criterion remain unresolved prerequisites to a prospective screen; quantum optimiser attribution comes later.

The thread ended at DRAFT, as specified by the brief. The enumerated source and second-model checks are complete. Their result is a descriptive failure of the tested decreasing transfer rule to improve on series means, with v2's opposite-direction signal retained. P's within-ligand optimiser comparison is not refuted by that cross-ligand result.\rr{joint entries 47 and 50}
